newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan plans $200-300 mln Eurobond issue.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan plans $200-300 mln Eurobond issue.

text.p: Kazakhstan plans to issue a $200-$300 mlilion Eurobond with a maturity of at least three years by the end of 1997, the head of the central bank said on Tuesday.

"We plan to raise $200-300 million on international capital markets," National Bank chairman Uraz Dzhandosov told a news conference. "Demand for Kazakh debt paper is great, the spread compared to December has fallen by one and half percentage points compared to similar paper in the Russian Federation."
Dzhandosov said he expected the oil-rich Central Asian state would be granted a higher credit rating for sovereign debt before its new Eurobond.
Last year Standard & Poor's and Moody's gave Kazakhstan respectively BB- and Ba3 ratings before its successful $200-million Eurobond debut.

Last year's issue -- placed in December and double the size of the originally planned one -- was snapped up by investors. The issue organised by Dutch bank ABN Amro Hoare Govett was initially priced to yield 9.3 percent, or 3.5 percentage points above comparable U.S. Treasury notes.

Dzhandosov said expectations of a better credit rating were backed by plans to slash further this year's inflation to 17 percent from 28.7 percent in 1996. Work on the international Caspian Pipeline Consortium building a link for Kazakh oil from the giant Tengiz field to the Russian Black Sea port of Novorossiisk was another factor, he said.

The Kazakh government said last month it was planning to raise $200-250 million in the summer with a Samurai bond -- a yen-denominated bond issued in Japan by a foreign borrower. But the plan has fallen through after talks between Kazakhstan and Japanese underwriters failed.
